preamble: The voiced alveolar affricate [dz] palatalizes to the alveolo-palatal [dʑ] before the high front vowel [i], as the tongue body rises toward the vowel. In Japanese, the voiced coronal (usually written /z/) is alveolo-palatal before /i/.

examples.from: 時間 じかん jikan 'time' (/z/ before /i/; [d͡z] before other vowels, e.g. ズボン [d͡zɨbõɴ])
examples.note: The phoneme, usually written /z/ and treated by some analysts as /dz/, varies between affricate and fricative; before /i/ it is alveolo-palatal.

examples.from: 文字 もじ moji 'letter, character'
